1: # OpenGlimpse — Project Documentation
2: # SCCCI Delegation Real-Time Facial Recognition Attendance System
3: # Problem Statement #10 | 4-Person Team
4: 
5: ---
6: 
7: ## 1. Project Overview
8: 
9: SCCCI (Singapore Chinese Chamber of Commerce & Industry) manages overseas business delegations of 15–30 (sometimes 100+) participants across multiple coaches and venues. Currently, headcount is taken manually by counting heads and doing roll calls — a slow, error-prone process that causes anxiety and programme overruns when someone is missing.
10: 
11: This system digitises and accelerates that process using a React-based mobile-first application with facial recognition as the primary attendance mechanism, supplemented by QR code scanning as a backup.
12: 
13: ---
14: 
15: ## 2. Use Case Definition
16: 
17: ### 2.1 Primary Use Case
18: **Title:** Real-Time Facial Recognition Attendance with Multi-Staff Sync
19: 
20: **Goal:** Allow SCCCI secretariat staff to take attendance for an overseas delegation in under 1 minute (30 pax) or 2 minutes (100+ pax) using facial recognition, with instant visibility of who is present or absent — across multiple staff devices simultaneously.
21: 
22: **Actors:**
23: - Staff / Secretariat (Primary) — takes attendance using facial recognition; can manually confirm identity if needed
24: - Trip Manager / Admin (Primary) — creates programmes, assigns staff, views consolidated real-time attendance, confirms departure readiness
25: - Delegate (Secondary) — identified via facial recognition as they enter coaches or venues
26: 
27: ### 2.2 Preconditions
28: - A programme has been created with a predetermined participant list
29: - Each delegate's facial photograph has been registered in the system (passport-sized photo)
30: - At least one staff member has the app open, is logged in, and is assigned to the current programme/route
31: - Internet connectivity (cellular data or hotspot) is available at the location for real-time cloud sync
32: - For first login by staff, updated facial photo is required to verify identity
33: 
34: ### 2.3 Main Flow (Happy Path)
35: 1. Admin creates a new programme with routes, bus assignments, and participant list.
36: 2. Staff member logs in with their account (verified by facial recognition on first login).
37: 3. Staff opens the attendance marking screen for their assigned route/coach.
38: 4. Delegate boards; staff activates live camera with facial detection. App displays bounding boxes around detected faces in real time.
39: 5. App matches detected face against stored delegate embeddings. If match confidence is high, delegate is marked Present automatically.
40: 6. If confidence is low or face is unrecognised, admin receives in-app alert. Staff can manually confirm identity from the list or use QR code backup.
41: 7. Attendance record syncs instantly to the cloud. All staff devices update in real time.
42: 8. The dashboard shows: Present list (with photos), Unidentified/Absent list (highlighted at top), and Ready-to-Depart status.
43: 9. When all delegates are accounted for, the Trip Manager confirms departure readiness.
44: 
45: ### 2.4 Alternative & Exception Flows
46: 
47: **Alt A — Low confidence facial match:**
48: - App flags confidence score and shows top candidate matches.
49: - Staff taps to confirm or manually selects from the list.
50: - Fallback: QR code scan on separate tab if delegate has badge.
51: 
52: **Alt B — Unidentified face:**
53: - Admin receives in-app alert for faces that don't match any registered delegate.
54: - Staff can manually add the person if it's a new arrival or late joiner.
55: - Photo quality may be poor — staff can request re-scan or use QR/manual override.
56: 
57: **Alt C — Manual attendance override:**
58: - Staff can always tap a delegate's name from the list to mark them Present or Absent.
59: - Covers roll calls when facial recognition is not available or delegate forgot badge.
60: 
61: **Alt D — Delegate joins/leaves programme mid-journey:**
62: - Admin amends the programme participant list on-the-fly from the app (add/remove delegate, change route/coach assignment).
63: 
64: **Alt E — Offline when scanning:**
65: - App queues facial scans locally (face image + embedding) if internet drops.
66: - When connectivity restores, queued scans are sent to backend for processing.
67: - Cloud data merges offline scans without loss or duplication.
68: 
69: ---
70:

83: | P1 | Programme & route creation — admin can set up trips, assign buses/routes, manage participant lists | XY / Matt |
84: | P1 | Staff account management — admin CRUD operations, staff login, face verification on first login | Matt |
85: | P1 | In-app alerts for unidentified faces — admin notified of FR matches below confidence threshold | Ryan / Backend |
86: | P1 | China-accessible hosting — app must not be blocked by Great Firewall | Backend |
87: | P2 | QR code backup scanning — delegate has QR on badge; staff can switch tab to scan if FR not possible | Ryan |
88: | P2 | Attendance summary & data aggregation — totals, pass rates, missing delegates report | XY |
89: | P2 | Ready-to-depart indicator — admin confirms all delegates accounted for before departure | XY |
90: | P2 | In-app chat & announcements — team members can communicate; announce updates with reactions | Rayhan |
91: | P2 | Navbar navigation — easy routing between Programme, Attendance, Profile, Chat sections | Rayhan |
92: | P3 | User profile management — staff can update personal info including new facial photo | Matt |
93: 
94: ---
95: 
96: ## 4. Tech Stack Details
97: 
98: ### 4.1 Frontend
99: - React web application with responsive design — optimised for staff smartphones and tablets
100: - Facial recognition: face-api.js library for real-time face detection, embedding generation, and similarity matching
101: - Camera API: device camera access with live face detection and bounding box visualization
102: - QR code scanner: separate tab with camera-based QR decoding (backup mode)
103: - Offline queue: browser localStorage for queuing facial scans and embeddings when disconnected
104: - UI: simple, high-contrast, glanceable — unidentified/absent delegates surfaced at top of list
105: 
106: ### 4.2 Backend
107: - Node.js REST API (Express.js) for programmes, routes, attendance, user management, and chat
108: - Real-time sync: WebSockets (Socket.io) for instant multi-device attendance updates and in-app chat
109: - Database: PostgreSQL — stores programmes, participants, facial embeddings (vectors), scan events, chat messages, user accounts
110: - Offline queue processing: backend receives offline scans, validates embeddings, and merges with live data without duplication
111: - Auth: staff login via JWT; delegate identity verified by facial embedding similarity
112: - Hosting: must be accessible from China — Alibaba Cloud (Singapore/Hong Kong region) strongly preferred
113: 
114: ### 4.3 Data & Privacy
115: - Delegate data: name, facial photograph (passport-sized JPEG), optional QR code ID, optional NFC tag ID
116: - Facial embeddings: stored in PostgreSQL as numeric vectors (face-api.js output); compared for similarity matching
117: - Staff data: account credentials, facial photo for login verification, permission levels
118: - Photos pre-registered by admin before the programme; staff updates own photo on first login
119: - Chat messages: retained for programme history; can be archived per admin policy
120: 
121: ### 4.4 Hardware (for Demo & Production)
122: - Development: laptop webcam acceptable with printed QR codes and mock data
123: - Final demo: mobile phone (Android/iOS) for live facial recognition, camera-based QR scanning
124: - QR badges: printed QR codes embedded in delegate badge lanyard
125: - NFC badges: optional for future enhancement; requires NFC-equipped phone
126: 
127: ---
128: 
129: ## 5. Integration Points
130: 
131: - Ryan calls: `POST /programmes/{id}/scans` with facial embedding + confidence
132: - XY calls: `PUT /programmes/{id}/attendance/{delegateId}` for manual mark present/absent
133: - Ryan & XY listen: WebSocket event `attendance:updated` to refresh dashboard in real time
134: - Rayhan manages: offline queue — client-side buffers scan payloads, backend deduplicates on sync
135: - Matt ensures: JWT tokens issued by auth endpoint are validated by all API consumers
136: 
137: ---
138: 
139: ## 6. Success Criteria
140: 
141: | Metric | Target |
142: |--------|--------|
143: | Time to reconcile 30 pax | < 1 minute |
144: | Time to reconcile 100+ pax | < 2 minutes |
145: | Facial recognition accuracy | ≥99% with staff confirmation for matches |
146: | Data loss on offline sync | Zero |
147: | Staff usability score | ≥4.5 / 5 |
148: | China accessibility | Fully functional on Alibaba Cloud; no GFW blocks |
149: | Cloud sync latency | < 2 seconds for multi-device updates |
150: 
151: ---
152: 
153: ## 7. Out of Scope
154: 
155: - Real-time location tracking or GPS maps (client uses WhatsApp)
156: - Liveness detection / anti-spoofing (client prioritises speed over security compliance)
157: - Government compliance audit trails
158: - Integration with external HR, CRM, or event management systems
159: - Push notifications beyond in-app alerts
160: - Voice calls or video conferencing (WhatsApp remains communication channel)
161: 
162: ---
163: 
164: ## 8. Assumptions & Risks
165: 
166: ### 8.1 Assumptions
167: - Internet (cellular data or hotspot) is available at all trip locations (China, ASEAN countries)
168: - Client will provide sample participant data: names + passport-sized facial photos
169: - Staff members have smartphones capable of running React web app (Android/iOS, modern browsers)
170: - Face-api.js embeddings are sufficient for matching with ≥99% accuracy among diverse delegate faces
171: - PostgreSQL with pgvector extension (or JSONB) is available on hosting provider
172: 
173: ### 8.2 Risks & Mitigation
174: 
175: | Risk | Mitigation |
176: |------|------------|
177: | Facial recognition accuracy on diverse faces, varied lighting, or poor photo quality | Set clear confidence thresholds (0.6+); always offer manual override; test with diverse delegation photos early |
178: | Great Firewall blocks Alibaba Cloud or host provider | Verify Alibaba Cloud Singapore/HK region connectivity from China SIM in Week 1; have AWS HK as backup |
179: | Face-api.js embedding format incompatible with backend matching algorithm | Agree on embedding format (size, normalization) in Week 1; test sample embeddings on both sides |
180: | WebSocket scaling — many concurrent staff devices cause latency | Load test early; consider Socket.io room/namespace for per-programme isolation |
181: | Offline queue duplication — same scan synced twice on reconnect | Add unique scan ID (timestamp + device ID) to each offline queue item; backend deduplicates on ID |
182: | QR code as backup underutilised if FR works well | Defer QR printing to P2; clients may choose not to use if FR is reliable |
183: 
184: ---
185: 
186: ## 9. Pages (UI)
187: 
188: - **Dashboard / Overview** — instant snapshot of delegate status; real-time counter (present/overall)
189: - **Scanner** — QR/NFC and facial scanning
190: - **Profile Page** — CRUD operations for delegate profiles
191: - **Support Tickets** — CRUD operations
192: - **Directory** — all delegates' name and info; manual check-in; notes (badge missing, verified manually)
193: - **Missing List** — shows who is missing; call button for direct contact; toggle for special occasions

1: # Offline-First Sync Engine Architecture
2: 
3: ## Project Context
4: 
5: This document outlines the architecture for a **sync engine** in an offline-first web application. The stack is:
6: 
7: - **Frontend:** React (browser)
8: - **Client-side DB:** IndexedDB via Dexie.js
9: - **Backend:** Node.js + Express
10: - **Server-side DB:** PostgreSQL via Sequelize
11: 
12: The goal is to allow end users to perform full **CRUD operations while offline**, with all changes automatically synced to the Postgres backend once connectivity is restored.
13: 
14: ---
15: 
16: ## High-Level Architecture
17: 
18: ```
19: React App
20:    |
21:    v
22: [Local DB: IndexedDB via Dexie.js]
23:    |  <-- reads cached data
24:    |  <-- writes go here + append change to pendingChanges
25:    v
26: [Sync Engine -- client-side]
27:    |  <-- accumulates offline changes as a single batch
28:    |  <-- on reconnect: POST batch to /sync, server returns full current state
29:    |  <-- client replaces local cache with server response
30:    v
31: [POST /sync (single endpoint)]
32:    |
33:    v
34: [Node.js + PostgreSQL via Sequelize]
35: ```
36: 
37: ### Data Flow Summary
38: 
39: 1. **Online reads:** Fetch from server, cache in Dexie `entities` table.
40: 2. **Offline reads:** Serve from Dexie `entities` table.
41: 3. **Offline writes:** Update entity in `entities` table, append a change entry to `pendingChanges.changes[]`.
42: 4. **On reconnect:** POST `{ lastSyncTimestamp, changes[] }` to `/sync`.
43: 5. **Server:** Applies each change (create/update/delete), queries all current records, returns full state.
44: 6. **Client:** Replaces local `entities` with server response, clears `pendingChanges`.
45: 
46: ### Conflict Resolution
47: 
48: **Batch-level last-write-wins.** The server applies client changes when the batch has content. On pull, the client always accepts the server's current state. If two devices are both offline and editing the same programme, the last device to sync "wins" — its changes overwrite the other's. For this app's use case (event management, typically one manager per programme), this is sufficient. Per-entity conflict resolution can be added later if needed.
49: 
50: ---
51: 
52: ## Technology Choices
53: 
54: ### Why IndexedDB (Dexie.js)
55: 
56: **Dexie.js** is the recommended choice because:
57: - It wraps IndexedDB with a clean, promise-based, near-SQL API.
58: - Data persists natively in the browser with no serialisation step.
59: - Zero build-tool complexity -- install and import.
60: - Works seamlessly with React.
61: - **Dexie core is free and open source.** Only Dexie Cloud (their hosted sync service) is paid -- we are not using that.
62: 
63: ---
64: 
65: ## Client-Side Data Model
66: 
67: ### Dexie Schema
68: 
69: ```js
70: import Dexie from 'dexie';
71: 
72: export const db = new Dexie('OpenGlimpseDB');
73: 
74: db.version(1).stores({
75:   entities:      'localId, serverId, type, status',
76:   pendingChanges: 'id'
77: });
78: ```
79: 
80: ### `entities` Table
81: 
82: Cached server data. Each record:
83: 
84: | Field | Type | Purpose |
85: |-------|------|---------|
86: | `localId` | UUID | Client-generated primary key (for reference before server assigns ID) |
87: | `serverId` | UUID / null | Server-assigned ID. `null` for pending creates. |
88: | `type` | string | Entity discriminator: `programme`, `route`, `delegate`, `attendance`, `readyToDepart` |
89: | `status` | enum | `synced` / `pending` / `deleted` |
90: | (domain fields) | varies | The actual record data (name, dates, status, etc.) |
91: 
92: ### `pendingChanges` Table
93: 
94: Always a single record (`id: 'current'`). Accumulates all offline modifications:
95: 
96: ```js
97: {
98:   id: 'current',
99:   changes: [
100:     { entityType: 'programme', op: 'create', data: { name, startDate, endDate } },
101:     { entityType: 'attendance', op: 'upsert', data: { programmeId, delegateId, status, method } },
102:     { entityType: 'delegate', op: 'update', serverId: 'uuid', data: { name } },
103:     { entityType: 'programme', op: 'delete', serverId: 'uuid' },
104:   ],
105:   timestamp: 1234567890
106: }
107: ```
108: 
109: **Change operations:**
110: - `create` -- insert a new entity (no `serverId` yet)
111: - `update` -- modify an existing entity (has `serverId`)
112: - `delete` -- soft-delete (marks entity as `deleted` locally)
113: - `upsert` -- create-or-update (used for attendance: one record per delegate per programme)
114: 
115: `pendingChanges` is cleared after each successful sync.
116: 
117: ---
118: 
119: ## Server-Side: Single `/sync` Endpoint
120: 
121: ### `POST /sync`
122: 
123: **Request body:**
124: ```js
125: {
126:   lastSyncTimestamp: number,  // client's last sync time (epoch ms)
127:   changes: [                  // empty array if client just wants to pull
128:     { entityType: string, op: string, serverId?: string, data: object }
129:   ]
130: }
131: ```
132: 
133: **Response:**
134: ```js
135: {
136:   programmes: [...],
137:   routes: [...],
138:   delegates: [...],
139:   attendance: [...],
140:   readyToDepart: [...],
141:   serverTimestamp: number
142: }
143: ```
144: 
145: **Server logic:**
146: 1. Iterate through `changes[]`, applying each one:
147:    - `create` -- insert into the appropriate table, return the server ID
148:    - `update` -- find by `serverId`, apply `data` fields
149:    - `delete` -- hard-delete by `serverId`
150:    - `upsert` -- find-or-create by programmeId + delegateId (for attendance)
151: 2. Query all current records for the 5 synced entity types
152: 3. Return full state + server timestamp
153: 
154: **No `updatedAt` columns needed on individual tables.** The server returns everything, the client replaces its cache. The `lastSyncTimestamp` is used only for logging/analytics, not for filtering.
155: 
156: ---
157: 
158: ## File Structure
159: 
160: ### Client-Side (`src/client/src/`)
161: 
162: ```
163: db/
164:   localDB.js                  # Dexie schema (2 tables)
165: sync/
166:   syncEngine.js               # pushAndPull() -- sends batch, replaces local cache
167:   offlineMutations.js         # Helper to append changes to pendingChanges
168: services/
169:   offlineApi.js               # Offline-aware wrappers for all API calls
170: hooks/
171:   useSync.js                  # App-root hook: triggers sync on reconnect + mount
172:   useConnectivity.js          # Exposes { isOnline, isSyncing, pendingCount }
173: components/shared/
174:   ConnectivityIndicator.jsx   # Online/offline/syncing banner
175: ```
176: 
177: ### Server-Side (`src/server/`)
178: 
179: ```
180: modules/sync/
181:   syncController.js           # POST /sync handler
182:   syncRoutes.js               # Route registration
183: ```
184: 
185: ### Modified Existing Files
186: 
187: | File | Change |
188: |------|--------|
189: | `src/client/src/App.jsx` | Mount `useSync()` + `ConnectivityIndicator` |
190: | `src/client/src/pages/directory/directory.jsx` | Swap imports to `offlineApi` |
191: | `src/client/src/pages/dashboard/dashboard.jsx` | Swap imports to `offlineApi` |
192: | `src/client/src/pages/programmes/ProgrammePage.jsx` | Swap imports to `offlineApi` |
193: | `src/client/src/pages/chat/chat.jsx` | Disable send when offline |
194: | `src/server/index.js` | Register sync routes |
195: 
196: ### No Changes Needed
197: 
198: | File | Reason |
199: |------|--------|
200: | `src/server/database/db.cjs` | No schema changes -- no `updatedAt` columns added |
201: | `src/client/src/services/api.js` | Stays as-is, used by `offlineApi.js` for online calls |
202: 
203: ---
204: 
205: ## What Each New File Does
206: 
207: | File | Purpose |
208: |------|---------|
209: | `db/localDB.js` | Dexie schema: `entities` (cached server data) + `pendingChanges` (batch of offline changes) |
210: | `sync/syncEngine.js` | `pushAndPull()` sends the pending batch to `/sync`, replaces local `entities` with the server response, clears `pendingChanges` |
211: | `sync/offlineMutations.js` | Helper functions (`createLocal`, `updateLocal`, `deleteLocal`, `upsertLocal`) that modify `entities` and append to `pendingChanges` in a Dexie transaction |
212: | `services/offlineApi.js` | Drop-in replacements for `services/api.js` functions. When online: fetch from server + cache. When offline: read from cache / write locally. |
213: | `hooks/useSync.js` | Mounted once at app root. Listens for `online` event, triggers `pushAndPull()`. Runs initial sync on mount. |
214: | `hooks/useConnectivity.js` | React hook returning `{ isOnline, isSyncing, pendingCount }`. Subscribes to connectivity monitor. |
215: | `components/shared/ConnectivityIndicator.jsx` | Full-width banner at top of viewport showing online/offline/syncing status |
216: | `modules/sync/syncController.js` | `POST /sync` handler: applies client changes, returns full current state |
217: | `modules/sync/syncRoutes.js` | Registers `POST /sync` on the Express app |
218: 
219: ---
220: 
221: ## Sync Sequence Diagram
222: 
223: ```
224: Client (offline)              Client (back online)           Server
225: -----------------             -------------------            ------
226: user checks in delegate
227:   -> update entity in Dexie
228:   -> append change to
229:      pendingChanges.changes[]
230:      (local UI updates immediately)
231: 
232:                               online event fires
233:                               -> pushAndPull()
234:                               -> read pendingChanges
235:                               -> POST /sync { changes[] } -> apply each change
236:                                                              to Postgres tables
237:                                  <- { programmes, routes,
238:                                        delegates, attendance,
239:                                        readyToDepart,
240:                                        serverTimestamp }
241:                               -> replace all entities
242:                                  in Dexie with response
243:                               -> clear pendingChanges
244:                               -> UI re-renders from
245:                                  fresh cached data
246: ```
247: 
248: ---
249: 
250: ## Design Decisions
251: 
252: 1. **Conflict strategy:** Batch-level last-write-wins. No per-entity `updatedAt` columns needed.
253: 2. **No endpoint mapping:** Single `/sync` endpoint handles all entity types. Server knows which table to write to based on `entityType`.
254: 3. **Pull is always full:** Server returns all records for the 5 synced entity types. Dataset is small (programmes + delegates + attendance for an event).
255: 4. **Chat offline:** Disabled entirely when offline. No message queueing.
256: 5. **Entity types synced:** programme, route, delegate, attendance, readyToDepart.
257: 6. **Entities NOT synced:** chat (real-time only), face recognition (requires Python server), auth (requires network for password hashing).
258: 7. **No `updatedAt` columns:** Server returns full state on every sync. Client replaces cache entirely.
259: 8. **Soft deletes not needed:** Hard deletes are fine because sync always returns full state.
260: 
261: ---
262:

### Full Contents of `sync-engine-architecture copy.md` (324 lines)

**Title:** "Offline-First Sync Engine Architecture"

This document is a comprehensive architectural plan for the offline sync engine. Key highlights:

- **Purpose:** Allow full CRUD operations while offline, with automatic sync to PostgreSQL once connectivity is restored.
- **Client-side DB:** IndexedDB via Dexie.js with two tables: `entities` (cached server data) and `pendingChanges` (batch of offline changes).
- **Server-side:** Single `POST /sync` endpoint that applies incoming changes and returns the full current state of all synced entity types.
- **Entity types synced:** `programme`, `route`, `delegate`, `attendance`, `readyToDepart`. Chat and facial recognition are NOT synced.
- **Conflict resolution:** Batch-level last-write-wins. The server applies client changes; on pull, the client always accepts the server's full state.
- **Detailed file structure** for both client-side (`db/localDB.js`, `sync/syncEngine.js`, `sync/offlineMutations.js`, `services/offlineApi.js`, `hooks/useSync.js`, `hooks/useConnectivity.js`, `components/shared/ConnectivityIndicator.jsx`) and server-side (`modules/sync/syncController.js`, `modules/sync/syncRoutes.js`).
